## Protocol 7: Rebuild Cube Session Table Index (Dry Run)

```
p7c --session-rebuild --dry-run --force-lock
```

## Command Breakdown

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--session-rebuild` | Targets the cube session table index for a full rebuild (not a delta update) |
| `--dry-run` | Performs a read-only simulation; no data is written or committed to the cube |
| `--force-lock` | Acquires a write lock on the cube session table to ensure no concurrent writes occur during the operation |

## How the Flags Work Together

- **`--session-rebuild`** tells the system to ignore the normal delta/patching mechanism and instead perform a complete index reconstruction.
- **`--dry-run`** runs the entire rebuild logic in read-only mode. This is useful for:
  - Estimating runtime and resource usage
  - Verifying index structure without side effects
  - Avoiding lock contention in a live environment
- **`--force-lock`** bypasses the normal non-blocking queue and forces an exclusive lock, ensuring the index rebuild runs in a quiescent state.

## Expected Output

Running the command in dry-run mode will print a summary similar to:

```
[Session Rebuild - Dry Run]
  - Target: cube_sessions
  - Estimated rows: 1,247,893
  - Estimated runtime: 4m 32s
  - Lock status: Would acquire write lock
  - Estimated disk I/O: 2.4 GB
  - Estimated memory: 384 MB
  - [Dry Run] No data will be modified.
```

## Use Cases

- **Pre-deployment validation** — verify the rebuild will complete within a maintenance window
- **Capacity planning** — estimate I/O and memory requirements
- **Safety check** — confirm the index is not already in a corrupted state before attempting a real rebuild
